1.
Heard Mr. Amit Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Mr. Rizean Ahmad, learned counsel for the State and perused the material on record.

2. The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant, Dharmendra Singh with a prayer to release him on bail in Case Crime No.141 of 2023, under sections 420, 120B, 304, 506 IPC,
Police Station ? Civil Lines, District ?Etawah, during pendency of trial.

sentences.text: As per the allegations in the FIR lodged on 14.06.2023 at about 13:00 hrs against three named accused including the applicant, on 16.06.2021 at about 08:00 am, the accused persons took the informant's brother; Lalbahadur on a motorcycle accompanied by Hakim Singh, Charan Singh and Sudama.
All the accused persons after making him drink alcohol, conspired to get sale deed executed on 16.06.2021 in favour of Rajnesh Kumar.
Rajnesh Kumar gave a cheque of one lac on the same day, which was dishonored, when the informant's brother placed the cheque before the concerned bank on the same date.
Due to the aforesaid fact, the informant's brother was tensed.
On 21.06.2021, the informant's brother went to file objection to the mutation proceedings before the Tehsildar.

When the aforesaid persons came to know about the aforesaid fact, they went to him and after intoxicating him by providing alcohol, they refused to give consideration amount for the sale deed as executed by informant's brother in favour of Rajnesh Kumar.
On 24.06.2021, the informant's brother expired due to consuming alcohol, which was provided by the accused persons.
Therefore, holding the accused persons responsible for administrating poisonous alcohol to the deceased, an application U/s 156(3) Cr.P.C.

was moved on 01.09.2021 by the informant, requesting for lodging the FIR and prior to that on 26.08.2021, the informant had approached the Senior Superintended of Police by way of posting a registered letter but nothing was done.

Subsequently,
the present FIR has been lodged through application U/s 156(3) Cr.P.C.
4.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case due to ulterior motive.
He further submits that the applicant is only a marginal witness of the sale deed executed in favour of Rajnaresh Kumar by the informant's brother; Lalbahadur.
He is no way involved in the incident.

In the FIR, nothing has been stated about the presence of the applicant on 23.06.2021, whereas allegation has come that all the accused persons administered poisonous alcohol, due to which the deceased expired.
He further submits that the deceased has died as he was suffering from TB.

In support of his contention, he has placed reliance upon the newspaper cutting, wherein it has been published that the deceased used to reside at his relative's house, namely, Ram Naresh and was suffering from some deceased, i.e. TB.
The deceased was taken to the District Hospital where the doctor declared dead.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant has also relied upon CD Parcha No.15, wherein the Investigating Officer came to the conclusion that the deceased was habitual drinker and he sold property in order to purchase alcohol and he had died due to consumption of alcohol.
Placing the postmortem report, he submits that no alcohol has been found and the cause of death could not be ascertained.
Hence, viscera was preserved.
Learned counsel for the applicant further placing reliance upon the inquest report submits that the boy, who brought the body of the deceased said that the death is due to vomiting of blood.
He further submits that there has been a delay of about two years in lodging the FIR and no plausible explanation has been given for the same.
The statement of witnesses, Hakim and Sudama have been recorded on 15.01.2024, hence it cannot be relied.
There is no evidence to connect the applicant in the present case.
Therefore, he is entitled to be released on bail.
He further submits that the criminal history of the applicant has been explained in para 7 to 11 of the rejoinder affidavit.
He is languishing in jail since 16.02.2024.
In case, he is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will cooperate in the trial by all means.
Lastly, it is submitted that there is no chance of applicant fleeing away from judicial process or tampering with the witnesses.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned AGA has vehemently opposed the prayer for bail by submitting that in the FIR itself the reason of delay has been given, wherein the letter was sent to the Senior Superintendent of Police through registered post on 26.08.2021 by the informant, but when nothing was done, she moved an application U/s 156(3) Cr.P.C., therefore, delay is well explained.

He further submits that in the FIR itself, it has been mentioned that on 16.06.2021, the deceased was accompanied by Haqim Singh, Charan Singh and Sudama as well as other accused persons and on 23.06.2021, all the aforesaid accused accompanied him when he had gone to move an objection in the mutation proceedings arising out of sale deed executed by him in favour of one Rajnaresh Kumar in which the applicant and co-accused-Ram Saran were marginal witnesses.
Conspiring part has also been mentioned in the FIR itself wherein all the accused persons conspired to get the property in favour of Rajnaresh Kumar.

He further submits that the statements of Haqim Singh and Sudama have been recorded by the Investigating Officer by way of affidavit on 15.01.2024, which is part of case dairy,
therefore, it is relevant.
In the aforesaid statements, it is clearly stated that all the accused persons were present on 23.06.2021 and they had given poisonous liquor to the deceased, which resulted in his death.
In the viscera report also Aluminum Phosphide has been found, copy of viscera report has been appended as Annexure No.C.A.-1 to the counter affidavit.

7. As regards the submission made by learned counsel for the applicant regarding presence of alcohol in the body of deceased while postmortem was conducted, learned AGA submits that the deceased was vomiting blood due to which alcohol could not be digested by the deceased.
The postmortem report shows that blood clot is present in the stomach.
As regards the newspaper cutting, which mentions that the deceased used to reside at his relative's house,
it is settled law that the newspaper cutting shall not be taken as an evidence.
He further submits that the applicant has committed heinous crime.
The statement of independent witnesses have been supported the prosecution story.
Hence, the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.

8. Taking into account the gravity of the offense, the evidence presented, the involvement of the accused, the severity of the punishment, and the arguments put forth by the learned counsel for both parties, I discern no compelling reason to exercise my discretion in favor of the accused applicant.
9. Accordingly, the bail application stands rejected.

10. It is clarified that the observations, if any, made in this order are strictly confined to the disposal of the bail application and must not be construed to have any reflection on the ultimate merits of the case.
